title: Are you comfortable with the work location / hybrid / remote model?
shortTitle: Are you comfortable with the work location / hybrid / remote model?
keyPoints: Be honest about your situation and flexible where you genuinely can be.
State any real constraint early and positively, with a plan to address it.
Frame in-office time as a positive for collaboration, not as a cost you tolerate.
Understand their model before answering: on-site, hybrid, or fully remote.
Show you understand why the model matters for a payments or fraud team.
Never over-promise something that will break in three months.
Confirm practical details: core hours, time-zone overlap, and office location.

s1_definition.oneliner: Be honest about your situation, flexible where you genuinely can be, and state any real constraint early and positively.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Honest flexibility** – Show you can adapt to their model without over-promising something unsustainable.
- **Positive framing** – Present in-office time as valuable for collaboration, not as a burden.
- **Early constraints** – Surface any real constraint (relocation timeline, caregiving) early with a clear plan.
- **Model awareness** – Understand the difference between on-site, hybrid, and remote before answering.
- **Team context** – Show you understand why the model matters for a payments team (incident coverage, design discussions).
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine Priya choosing a bank branch at National Bank of India. If the branch is open only on weekdays and she can only visit weekends, there is a mismatch : better to surface it early than discover it after opening the account. But if she says "I can come any day, and I even prefer in-person for big transactions", the relationship works smoothly.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Yes, I am comfortable with your hybrid model at National Bank of India, and I actually see the in-office days as a positive rather than a cost. Three days in the office works well for me : I find in-person time genuinely valuable for design discussions, incident coordination, and building rapport with the team, and I am equally productive remotely for focused, deep-work tasks.

I also want to be straightforward about my situation rather than leave anything to surprise you later. I can commit fully to being on-site, and if there is anything that affects timing I would tell you upfront with a plan. I would never say yes to a model I could not actually sustain, because that only creates a problem a few months down the line.

I understand why the model matters to you as well. On a payments or fraud team there are periods where in-person coverage really helps, especially during incidents, and I am happy to be present when the team needs it rather than treating the policy as a rigid personal entitlement.

The reason I answer this way is that this question is checking logistical fit and whether I am flexible and honest. I confirm I can meet your model, I frame the in-office element positively, I surface any genuine constraint early with a plan, and I show I understand why the model matters to the team.

Remember one sentence: Be honestly flexible about work location, frame in-office time as valuable, and surface any constraint early with a clear plan.
